text.p: RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd announced a management restructure on Wednesday.
The following is a full text of that announcement.
"RTZ-CRA is re-organising its management structure into six new global product businesses. These new RTZ-CRA businesses will be among the world leaders in their respective sectors internationally.
The leadership of three of the global businesses will be based in London and three in Australia. They will be supported by a worldwide technology group.

Group Headquarters will remain in London. The Group's Melbourne office will be substantially restructured and its role changed to one of support for the three product businesses based in Australia, together with the fulfilment of statutory obligations.
Kennecott Corporation's Salt Lake City, Utah office will be closed and some support services transferred to Kennecott Utah Copper.
The six businesses, together with the worldwide exploration and technology groups, will report to Mr Leon Davis, RTZ-CRA's Chief Executive.
They are:
Aluminium (Comalco) Terry Palmer
Brisbane Copper Jonathan Leslie
London Energy Leigh Clifford
Melbourne Gold and Other Minerals John Collier
London Industrial minerals Gordon Sage
London Iron ore Mick O'Leary*
Perth Exploration David Klingner
London Technology Oscar Groeneveld London
* Following Mr O'Leary's retirement in September 1997, the iron ore business will be headed by Mr Chris Renwick.
Goup operations will continue to trade under their present business names.
Mr Leon Davis, RTZ-CRA's Chef Executive, said; "Following the merger of RTZ and CRA, our organisation was mainly on a geographical basis.

Whilst retaining our devolved management philosophy, the new product-based organisation not only brings a keener focus on customers and opportunities, but simplifies relationships, better concentrates our technological expertise and streamlines decision making.
It sharpens our business and makes us more competitive by achieving efficiency gains and cost savings."

Mr Robert Wilson, Executive Chairman, said; "This is a major step in furthering the process of integration between RTZ and CRA to enable us to realise the full benefits of the merger of 15 months ago.
In the enlarged group it has become ever more important to avoid unnecessary layers in the organisation structure and this we are doing in Australia, North America and elsewhere.
It will facilitate a clearer focus on business unit performance and our prime objective of creating long-term shareholder value."
As previously announced, RTZ-CRA will become Rio Tinto in May of this year, subject to approval at the Annual General Meetings of RTZ and CRA.
RTZ-CRA GLOBAL RE-ORGANISATION AUSTRALIAN ARRANGEMENTS
Commenting in Melbourne on the global re-organisation announced today, the Chief Executive of RTZ-CRA, Mr Leon Davis, outlined the major implications and details of the Australian arrangements.

Three of the six global businesses will be based in Australia. In addition, the worldwide exploration and technology groups in London will be led by Australians, while the world centre for R&D will be located in Australia," Mr Davis said.
"The move of Comalco to Brisbane and the locating of RTZ-CRA Iron Ore in Perth acknowledges the establishment of Queensland and Western Australia as world centres of the mining industry."

Mr Davis said that Mr Leigh Clifford, who has successfully led the integration of CRA into the global Group, will head the new RTZ-CRA Energy business from Melbourne. He will be responsible for managing world class coal and uranium operations in Australia, North America, Latin America, Indonesia and Namibia.

"This business alone represents enormous potential for the worldwide Group. Bringing all of our coal assets under a single management will facilitate the introduction of world's best practice standards to the Australian coal industry," Mr Davis said.
The iron ore group will be headed by Mr Mick O'Leary and after his retirement in September, by Mr Chris Renwick. Comalco will continue to be headed by Mr Terry Palmer.
The combined interests of the Australian-based operations will have high-level representation through an office in Melbourne headed by Dr Ian Gould, who will report to Mr Davis.

The Melbourne office will provide the Australian-based businesses with shared local support services including human resources, external affairs, legal, taxation and treasury and continue to meet the necessary listing requirements of the Australian Stock Exchange.
It will also assist the businesses in implementing the Group's policies in Aboriginal and community affairs, the environment and employee relations.
Unfortunately, about half of the jobs in the Melbourne office will disappear as a result of the restructure.
Some of the remaining positions will be transferred to operating locations.
In the case of those leaving, the Group will provide both practical and financial assistance to help their transition."
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
